title: Level-Pool (Modified Puls) Routing — Storage Indication

subscripts 1,2.description: Beginning and end of time step

applicability: Valid for reservoirs where water surface is approximately horizontal. Requires elevation-storage and elevation-discharge curves.

title: Reservoir Storage-Elevation Relationship (Approximation)
equation: S = a × (h - h₀)^b  or  S = Σ[(A_i + A_{i+1})/2 × Δh_i] (prismoidal)

A_i.description: Surface area at elevation i (from contour map or DEM)

a, b.description: Regression constants from site-specific area-capacity survey

title: PMP Moisture Maximization Ratio

W_max.description: Maximum precipitable water for the location and season (from 100-year persisting 12-hr dewpoint)

W_storm.description: Precipitable water during the observed storm (from representative dewpoint)

applicability: Storm transposition technique. Ratio W_max/W_storm typically 1.2–1.8. Applied to individual controlling storms, then envelope the results.

title: USBR Simplified Peak Breach Outflow

Hw.description: Height of water above breach invert at time of failure

applicability: Regression from historical dam failures. Quick screening estimate. For detailed analysis, use Froehlich (2008) or NWS BREACH model.

Vw.description: Reservoir volume at time of failure

Hw.description: Height of water above breach invert

k₀.description: Overtopping coefficient: 1.3 for overtopping, 1.0 for piping

Vw.description: Reservoir volume at time of breach

Hb.description: Breach height (typically full dam height for embankments)

Vw.description: Reservoir volume at time of breach

title: Broad-Crested Weir Outflow (Breach or Spillway)

Q.description: Discharge through breach or over spillway

B.description: Breach width or spillway crest length

H.description: Head above weir crest or breach invert

applicability: Used in breach models and spillway rating curves. US customary: Q = C_L × B × H^1.5 with C_L in ft^0.5/s (typically 2.6–3.1).

title: Reservoir Attenuation (Rule of Thumb)

V_inflow.description: Total inflow volume of flood event

applicability: If S_flood/V_inflow is large (>0.3), significant attenuation occurs. If small (<0.05), minimal attenuation — outflow ≈ inflow. Used for preliminary sizing only. Formal routing required for design.

title: DV Product — Life Safety Criterion
applicability: DV < 0.3 m²/s: low hazard (wading possible). 0.3–0.5: moderate (adults at risk). 0.5–1.0: high (structural damage to light buildings). >1.0: extreme (destruction of wood-frame structures). Used in dam breach consequence assessment and EAPs.
source: USBR Downstream Hazard Classification, ANCOLD, Clausen & Clark (1990)
